title: Over a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain, residue field extensions in a finite extension of fraction fields are finite
statement: Let $\varphi:R\to S$ be an injective homomorphism of integral domains, with fraction fields $K$ of $R$ and $L$ of $S$, so that $\varphi$ induces a field extension $K\subseteq L$ [def-pc-field-extension]; assume $\dim_KL<\infty$. Assume $R$ is a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] local ring with maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ and Krull dimension $1$ [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Then (1) every prime ideal $\mathfrak n\subset S$ with $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak m$ is a maximal ideal of $S$; (2) there are only finitely many such prime ideals; (3) for each of them the residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak n)=S_{\mathfrak n}/\mathfrak nS_{\mathfrak n}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], which is a field extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak m)=R/\mathfrak m$ through $\varphi$, is finite-dimensional over $\kappa(\mathfrak m)$.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 031F (lemma-finite-extension-residue-fields-dimension-1, line 29241), statement. Tag verified in tags/tags: 031F,algebra-lemma-finite-extension-residue-fields-dimension-1

proof.text: Give S its R-algebra structure via φ. A local domain of dimension one is not a field (Mathlib ringKrullDim_eq_zero_of_isField), so its maximal ideal m contains a nonzero x. Give L its R-action through K; hcompat makes the R,S,L tower commute. Compose S → L with the coordinate equivalence of a finite K-basis of L. This is an injective R-linear map, identifying S with a submodule M of K^r. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-dim-one-submodule-quotient-finite-length] to M and x, and transport finite length along QuotSMulTop.congr to S/xS.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 031F (lemma-finite-extension-residue-fields-dimension-1), proof, first two sentences; Lemma Tag 00PE (lemma-finite-length)

proof.text: Work directly with the tensor closed fibre B = κ(m) ⊗_R S. Since m is maximal, R → κ(m) is surjective, so S → B, s ↦ 1 ⊗ s, is surjective (Mathlib includeRight_surjective). Multiplication by x is zero on B, so this R-linear map factors through S/xS. Finite length descends along this surjection (IsFiniteLength.of_surjective), hence B is Noetherian over R and finitely generated over R. Enlarging scalars makes B finitely generated over κ(m), by Module.Finite.of_restrictScalars_finite. This proves the finite-dimensional closed fibre claim, including B = 0.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 031F, proof, sentences 3-5; Lemma Tag 00IY (lemma-dimension-is-length)

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dim-algebra-artinian], B is Artinian. Mathlib IsArtinianRing.isPrime_iff_isMaximal and the Finite (PrimeSpectrum B) instance give maximality and finiteness of its primes directly. PrimeSpectrum.preimageEquivFiber R S ⟨m, inferInstance⟩ identifies this finite spectrum with the primes n of S with comap φ n = m. Its inverse takes comap under the surjection S → B. Maximal ideals pull back to maximal ideals under a surjection (Ideal.comap_isMaximal_of_surjective), so every such n is maximal. Transport Finite across the equivalence and rewrite the subtype condition to prove Set.Finite of the fibre.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 031F, proof, sentences 5-7; Lemmas Tags 00J6 and 00JB

proof.text: For n over m, use its proved maximality. Equip κ(n) with the algebra structure of the statement using Ideal.ResidueField.map m n φ hn.symm. The map identity on κ(m) and S → κ(n) agree on R by Ideal.ResidueField.map_algebraMap, so the tensor-product universal property gives a κ(m)-linear algebra map B → κ(n). It is surjective: maximality of n makes S → κ(n) surjective, and a lift s gives the tensor 1 ⊗ s. Thus Module.Finite.of_surjective applied to this map proves the exact finite-dimensional residue extension in the statement.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 031F, proof, final sentence
